q: What is the matching height for the given base of this parallelogram?
img:
<svg viewBox="0 0 380 220" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="width:100%;max-width:420px">
  <path d="M60,170 L260,170 L320,50 L120,50 Z" fill="#EEF1F8" stroke="#2B3242" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
  <line x1="320" y1="50" x2="320" y2="170" stroke="#2B3242" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6,5"/>
  <rect x="308" y="158" width="12" height="12" fill="none" stroke="#2B3242" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="15" y="115" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#2B3242">5 in.</text>
  <text x="155" y="200" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#2B3242">10 in.</text>
  <text x="326" y="115" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#4F46E5">h in.</text>
  <text x="60" y="25" font-size="16" font-weight="800" fill="#2B3242">Area: 40 square inches</text>
</svg>
why: Area = base × height. The area is 40 square inches and the base is 10 inches, so height = 40 ÷ 10 = 4 inches. The 5 in. side is a slanted side, not the height — it isn’t used in the area formula.
tip: For a parallelogram, always use the height that is perpendicular to the base — a slanted side length is a distractor, not the height.

q: A triangle has an area of 12 square units. Which base and height could it have?
why: Triangle area = (base × height) ÷ 2. For base 8 and height 3: (8 × 3) ÷ 2 = 12. The other pairs give 8, 9, and 10 square units.
tip: There are many base/height pairs that give the same triangle area — check each with (base × height) ÷ 2 rather than assuming there’s only one right answer.

q: Triangle 1 has a base of 6 units and Triangle 2 has a base of 8 units. Both triangles have an area of 12 square units. What is the height of each triangle?
tip: Work the triangle area formula backwards — multiply the area by 2 before dividing by the base, so you don’t forget the factor of 2.

q: This pentagon is a rectangle with a triangular roof. The base is 8 cm, the vertical walls are 6 cm, and the total height from the base to the peak is 9 cm. What is the area of the pentagon?
img:
<svg viewBox="0 0 320 240" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="width:100%;max-width:420px">
    <path d="M70,218 L246,218 L246,86 L158,20 L70,86 Z" fill="#EEF1F8" stroke="#2B3242" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
    <line x1="158" y1="20" x2="158" y2="218" stroke="#2B3242" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6,5"/>
    <rect x="152" y="206" width="12" height="12" fill="none" stroke="#2B3242" stroke-width="1.5"/>
    <text x="166" y="119" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#4F46E5">9 cm</text>
    <text x="24" y="157" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#2B3242">6 cm</text>
    <text x="252" y="157" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#2B3242">6 cm</text>
    <text x="134" y="240" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#2B3242">8 cm</text>
  </svg>
why: Split it into a rectangle and a triangle. Rectangle: 8 × 6 = 48. The triangle’s height is the total height minus the wall height: 9 − 6 = 3, so its area is (8 × 3) ÷ 2 = 12. Total: 48 + 12 = 60 square centimeters.
tip: For a composite "house" shape, split it into a rectangle plus a triangle — and remember the triangle’s own height is only the part above the rectangle, not the whole figure’s height.

q: A polyhedron has 2 parallel, congruent triangular faces connected by 3 rectangular faces. What is it called?
why: A prism is named by the shape of its two parallel, congruent bases. Triangular bases connected by rectangles make a triangular prism.
tip: A prism’s name comes from its base shape; a pyramid instead has triangular faces meeting at a single point (an apex), not a second parallel base.

q: Sadie is going to paint the front of her house, shown here. What is the area of the front of her house?

<svg viewBox="0 0 360 240" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="width:100%;max-width:420px">

    <rect x="169" y="176" width="12" height="12" fill="none" stroke="#2B3242" stroke-width="1.5"/>
    <text x="183" y="104" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#4F46E5">12 ft</text>
    <text x="24" y="151" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#2B3242">6 ft</text>
    <text x="286" y="151" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#2B3242">6 ft</text>
    <text x="151" y="210" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#2B3242">15 ft</text>
  </svg>
why: Split the house into a rectangle and a triangle. Rectangle: 15 × 6 = 90. The triangle’s height is 12 − 6 = 6, so its area is (15 × 6) ÷ 2 = 45. Total: 90 + 45 = 135 square feet.
tip: For a house-shaped composite figure, the total height given usually includes the wall — subtract the wall height first to get the roof triangle’s own height.

q: The front of Sadie’s house is 135 square feet, and the back is the same shape. She has enough paint in one case to cover 100 square feet. How many cases of paint will she need to paint the front AND back?
why: Front + back = 135 + 135 = 270 square feet. 270 ÷ 100 = 2.7, but paint only comes in whole cases, so she must round up to 3 cases — 2 cases wouldn’t be quite enough.
tip: When a real-world total doesn’t divide evenly, round up if you can only buy whole units (cases, buses, boxes) — even a small leftover amount needs one more.

tip: Surface area formula for a rectangular prism: 2(lw + lh + wh) — or just add up all 6 faces of the net one at a time.
